PTFE Sheets · Manufacturer

PTFE Sheets & Slabs

Moulded and skived PTFE (Teflon) sheets in virgin and filled grades — supplied as sheet, cut blanks or finished gaskets for sealing, lining, sliding and insulating applications.

Request a Quote WhatsApp

PTFE sheet is the most versatile form of the material: it is the stock that gaskets, washers, slide bearings, tank linings and insulating barriers are cut from. Choosing the right sheet comes down to three things — how it is made, which grade it is, and the thickness you need.

Moulded vs skived PTFE sheet

PTFE cannot be melt-processed like most plastics, so sheet is produced in one of two ways:

  • Moulded sheet — PTFE powder is compressed in a mould and sintered. This route suits thicker sections and blocks, and is the usual choice when you will machine the sheet further or need a thick slide pad.
  • Skived sheet — a thin, continuous layer is peeled from a rotating moulded billet. Skiving gives uniform thin sheet and film with a smooth surface, well suited to gaskets, liners and electrical insulation.

For bonded applications — for example lining a vessel or bonding a slide pad to a steel plate — PTFE sheet can be etched on one or both faces so adhesives can grip what is otherwise a non-stick surface.

Grades of PTFE sheet

Virgin PTFE gives the best chemical resistance and electrical properties. Filled grades trade a little of that for higher compressive strength, better wear resistance and less creep under load — important for gaskets that see bolt load and for sliding pads.

General guidance from published data. Filler percentages vary between compounds — confirm the exact grade for your application. *Ask for compliance documentation for food or pharma contact before ordering.
GradeWhat it changesWatch-outsTypical uses
Virgin PTFEHighest purity; best chemical resistance and electrical insulationLowest compressive strength; most prone to creep (cold flow)Chemical service, electrical insulation, food and pharma contact parts*
Glass-filled
commonly 15–25 %		Better compressive strength and wear resistance; less creepAbrasive to soft mating surfaces; glass is attacked by hydrofluoric acid and hot strong alkalisValve seats, seals, gaskets, structural pads
Carbon-filled
often ~25 %, may include graphite		High compressive strength and wear resistance; better thermal conductivity; antistaticNot an electrical insulatorPiston rings, seals and bearings in water, steam and dry gas
Bronze-filled
commonly 40–60 %		Best creep and wear resistance; highest thermal conductivityReduced chemical resistance (acids, ammonia); electrically conductiveHydraulic seals and guide rings, bearings, wear strips
Graphite-filled
commonly 5–15 %		Lower friction and good dry-running behaviourLower strength than carbon- or bronze-filledBushes and seals running against softer shafts

Not sure which grade fits? Our guide to virgin vs filled PTFE walks through the trade-offs.

Applications

  • Gaskets and washers — flange gaskets, rings and washers cut from sheet for chemical, pharmaceutical and food processing lines. See PTFE gaskets.
  • Linings — tank, chute and hopper linings where corrosion resistance or non-stick release matters.
  • Slide and wear pads — low-friction bearing pads for structural expansion joints, pipe supports and machine slideways.
  • Electrical insulation — barriers, spacers and insulating washers that rely on PTFE’s low dielectric constant and high resistivity.
  • Anti-stick surfaces — heat-sealing, moulding and food-handling surfaces where product must release cleanly.

Typical properties of virgin PTFE

Typical values for unfilled (virgin) PTFE, compiled from published material data. Actual values depend on resin, processing and test method — they are a design guide, not a specification for a particular lot.
Density2.14 – 2.20 g/cm³
Continuous service temperatureapprox. −200 °C to +260 °C
Crystalline melting pointapprox. 327 °C
Tensile strengthapprox. 20 – 35 MPa
Elongation at breakapprox. 250 – 400 %
Hardnessapprox. 50 – 60 Shore D
Coefficient of friction (dynamic, on steel)approx. 0.05 – 0.10
Dielectric constant (1 MHz)approx. 2.1
Water absorption (24 h)< 0.01 %
Thermal expansionhigh — roughly ten times that of steel at room temperature
Flammabilitydoes not sustain combustion in air (limiting oxygen index above 95 %)

Two properties deserve attention when designing with sheet: PTFE creeps (cold-flows) under sustained load, and it has a high thermal expansion. Both are why filled grades are often preferred for gaskets and load-bearing pads. More detail in our PTFE properties guide.

What to include in your enquiry

  1. Grade — virgin or filled (or the operating conditions, and we will suggest one).
  2. Thickness, sheet size or cut dimensions, and tolerance if critical.
  3. Quantity, and whether this is a one-off or repeat requirement.
  4. Any finishing — etching, cutting to a gasket drawing, or machining.
  5. The application: media, temperature and pressure help us recommend the right material.

Common Questions

PTFE Sheet FAQs

Questions buyers commonly ask before ordering PTFE sheet.

Ask a Question

Teflon™ is a brand name (Chemours) for PTFE. “Teflon sheet” and “PTFE sheet” are used interchangeably in industry to mean sheet made from polytetrafluoroethylene. We supply PTFE sheet; we do not claim it is the branded product.

Skived sheet is usually the better choice for thin gauges, gaskets and liners because it is uniform and smooth. Moulded sheet suits thicker sections and material that will be machined. Tell us the thickness and application and we will recommend one.

Untreated PTFE is very difficult to bond. Sheet that has been chemically etched on one or both faces can be bonded with suitable adhesives — specify etched sheet in your enquiry.

Virgin PTFE offers the widest chemical resistance but creeps under bolt load. Filled grades (for example glass-filled) resist creep better. For uneven or fragile flanges, softer gasket constructions are often used. Our gasket selection guide covers the options.

Yes. We supply full sheets and also cut strips, blanks, rings and gaskets to your dimensions or drawing.
